items.title: Friday Squid Blogging: Bigfin Squid Off California Coast
items.summary: Neat video : The sighting, announced September 2, marks the first time anyone has spotted a live bigfin squid, which belongs to the Magnapinna genus, in the northeastern Pacific Ocean. As usual, you can also use this squid post to talk about the security stories in the news that I haven’t covered. Blog moderation policy.

items.title: Studying Fraudulent North Korean IT Workers
items.summary: Researchers set up a fake start-up company to study fraudulent North Korean IT workers.

items.title: Hiding Capabilities in AI Models
items.summary: Interesting research: “ AI Models Can Provably Hide Arbitrary Capabilities ” Abstract: Capability evaluations aim to surface dangerous model behaviors before deployment, but their reliability depends on the assumption that hidden capabilities can be elicited. We show this assumption does not hold under adversarial conditions by constructing backdoor attacks…

items.title: Friday Squid Blogging: Increasing Squid Populations
items.summary: This article in Nature argues that it’s due to an overfishing of predators and warming sea temperatures. As usual, you can also use this squid post to talk about the security stories in the news that I haven’t covered. Blog moderation policy.

items.title: New Serious PHP Vulnerabilities Released and Patched
items.summary: PHP maintainers have released fixes for two critical vulnerabilities: PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 fix two critical vulnerabilities that can allow unauthenticated remote code execution. items.title: Workshop on Economics and Information Security (WEIS) Archive
items.summary: There’s a new archive of all the papers from twenty-five years of the Workshop on Economics and Information Security (WEIS). Really nice resource. It’s fun to reread my 2002 essay on the economics of information security.
